description:
This is a non-motorized trail.
The Mark Berger Traverse is named after a man who played a great part in establishing the hiking club in the Vernon area . 1944-1989. There is a small monument to Mark Berger near Monasahee Lake via the Monashee Lake Trail. The traverse is a mountaineering effort although the access from Twin Lakes is easier for a start. Both sides have areas for undeveloped mountain camping. There are no facilities so pack out what you pack in. The access point from Monashee Lake Trail is very rugged and not definitively marked. This trail should be considered with extensive experience.
directions:
The South Fork Forest Service Road is a radio-controlled road. It is a busy industrial road. All road users are advised to exercise extreme caution and follow posted resource road protocol.
Learn more about: Okanagan Shuswap Natural Resource District Road safety information
Access is via Monashee Creek Trail or Twin Lakes Trail , driving directions are on the RSTBC WEB.
title: Mark Berger Traverse
